title: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)

sections.label: Singapore law and order rankings
sections.summary: Singapore ranked first in the Gallup Global Law and Order Report 2020 and first for order and security in the World Justice Project's Rule of Law Index 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the Gallup Global Law and Order Report 2020, Singapore was ranked first for the seventh year running.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the World Justice Project's Rule of Law Index 2020, Singapore was ranked first in the area of "order and security".

sections.label: Terrorist threat and self-radicalisation
sections.summary: The terrorist threat Singapore faces remains as high as about 20 years ago, and ISD recently thwarted a self-radicalised youth's plans to attack two mosques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Technology gives a new twist to old threats too – for example, the terrorist threat Singapore faces today remains as high as it was about 20 years ago when ISD thwarted Jemaah Islamiah's plans to attack an MRT station and several foreign embassies in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Just a few weeks ago, ISD once again thwarted the plans of a youth who became self-radicalised through online sources and intended to attack two mosques on the anniversary of the Christchurch mosque attacks.

sections.label: Officers as hyper-humans
sections.summary: The challenge is to make a transformational change so officers undertake duties as hyper-humans with sensor systems, CCTV, live feeds and police cameras.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The challenge now, given the drivers for change, is to make an even more transformational change, so that these officers undertake their duties not as mere mortals, but what I term as hyper-humans – with eyes and ears of sensor systems, closed circuit television, live feeds and police cameras.

sections.label: COVID-19 police technology opportunity
sections.summary: In a COVID-19 environment with less public gatherings and large MICE events, the police force has an opportunity to evaluate better technology use in daily operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Especially in a COVID-19 environment, there will be greater stress and strain on operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, with less public gatherings and less large MICE events, the police force now have an opportunity to evaluate how technology can be better utilised in the day-to-day ops of the force.

sections.label: Police technology during pandemic
sections.summary: The question asks how the police force tapped technology to overcome pandemic operational constraints and how this can be developed for a post-pandemic world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: How has the police force tapped on technology to overcome any operational constraints presented by the pandemic, and how can this be continued to be developed and improved on as we move into a post-pandemic world?

sections.label: ICA manpower during COVID-19
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry and ICA managed unusual manpower requirements amid mostly closed borders and additional controls and paperwork.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, I would like to find out how the Ministry and in particular, the ICA, has managed the unusual manpower requirements in the current COVID-19 situation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the one hand, borders are mostly closed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But on the other hand, additional controls and paperwork mean officers may need to be redeployed or additional manpower may be engaged.

sections.label: Digitalisation can be regressive
sections.summary: Digitalisation of services can be regressive when it makes going online harder for the less well off, less literate and less IT savvy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, even with the best of policy intentions, it can be regressive, when digitalisation of services makes it harder for the less well off, less literate, less IT savvy to go online.

sections.label: Non-Internet users and computerless households
sections.summary: In 2019, 11% of individuals were non-Internet users and 11% of resident households had no computers, with some residents told to seek help elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Infocomm Media Development Authority's statistical data shows in 2019, 11% of individuals are non-Internet users and there are still 11% of resident households that are without computers, including desktop, laptops, notebooks and tablets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some residents shared that they had approached ICA officers to seek assistance, but was advised to turn to relatives, friends, or alternatively, to approach immigration agents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand that Malaysian agents charge a fee of between $300 and $400, which is indeed a huge sum, especially for low-income groups.

sections.label: Marriages between Singaporeans and foreigners
sections.summary: About one in three Singapore marriages is between a Singaporean and a non-Singaporean, and foreigners married to Singaporeans can apply for an LTVP or LTVP+.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Around one in three marriages in Singapore is between a Singaporean and a non-Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, foreigners married to Singaporeans can apply for a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP), or an LTVP+.

sections.label: Video recording of police interviews
sections.summary: After the Parti Liyani case debate, the Minister for Home Affairs promised improvements, and it was asked what is being done to speed up video recording of police interviews.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, during the debate on the Parti Liyani’s case, the Minister for Home Affairs has promised some improvements to the police investigation process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We would like to know: what is being done to speed up the implementation of the video recording system for police interviews of accused persons?

sections.label: Reassurances after radicalised youth arrest
sections.summary: Following the arrest of a radicalised 16-year-old Christian youth who plotted mosque attacks, the Minister of State for Home Affairs gave reassurances on steps to counter radical threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, following the announcement this year of the arrest of the 16-year-old radicalised Christian youth who plotted terror attacks at two mosques, it was important to hear the reassurances from the Minister of State for Home Affairs – that the authorities have taken increased steps to reach out to youth through social media and other means to counter radical threats.

sections.label: Religious harmony and laws
sections.summary: It was asked whether laws and policies could tilt towards particular religious beliefs, and suggested revisiting the 1989 White Paper on the Maintenance of Religious Harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is there a danger in Singapore that laws and policies could be tilted towards particular religious beliefs, for example, because of the dominant religious beliefs of senior civil servants, or people of influence, if not now, maybe sometime in future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This may be a good time to revisit the 1989 White Paper on the Maintenance of Religious Harmony, which was a very different time in terms of interpersonal communication.

sections.label: Secularism and communal harmony rules
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will restate or update working rules and laws to preserve strict secularism in Singapore's multi-racial, multi-religious society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Beyond a new White Paper or Maintenance of Harmony White Paper updated to identify the key dangers to communal harmony in Singapore for this generation, will the Government consider a restatement or an update of its working rules and laws to ensure that there is preservation of strict secularism, so that all communities recognise that no one is placed above the other in matters of law, policy and governance in our multi-racial and multi-religious society which also increasingly holds other communities.

sections.label: Singapore's vulnerability to interference
sections.summary: States that Singapore is especially vulnerable because of its openness, multi-racial society and global interconnectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Singapore is especially vulnerable because of our openness, our multi-racial society and global interconnectivity.

sections.label: MHA deterring foreign interference
sections.summary: Asks how MHA is equipping itself to stave off and deter foreign interference and influence in domestic affairs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: How is MHA equipping itself to stave off and deter such foreign interference and influence in our domestic affairs?

sections.label: Youths, extremism and rehabilitation
sections.summary: Cites an IPS paper on youths open to religious extremists online, a detained youth influenced by the Christchurch attack, and a rehabilitated youth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: An Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) paper in 2019 found that almost half of youths aged 18 to 25 are open to religious extremists publishing their views on the Internet or social media.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Fresh on everyone's mind was the timely discovery and detention of a Singaporean youth who was influenced by the 2019 Christchurch attack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: On the other hand, a self-radicalised Muslim youth went from being an ISIS supporter in 2017, to becoming a star student for his GCE "N" levels in 2021 following successful rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: What is in common is, that both of these youths were assessed to have a weak understanding of Islam.

sections.label: Instalment payments for traffic fines
sections.summary: Notes the Minister's view that the fine framework should stay intact, and calls for instalment payments for first-time low-income traffic offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: In response, the Minister for Home Affairs mentioned, he is of the view that the fine framework should be kept intact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: I am calling upon Minister to reconsider in allowing instalment payments for traffic fines specifically for first-time offenders that belongs to the low-income group and our beneficiaries of Government's financial assistance scheme such as ComCare.

sections.label: Security Industry Digital Plan stages
sections.summary: States that the 2018 Security Industry Digital Plan outlined a digital roadmap identifying three stages of technology for security agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: The Security Industry Digital Plan launched in 2018 outlined a digital roadmap that identified three stages of technology that security agencies can adopt.

sections.label: Security officers abuse survey
sections.summary: A survey found one in three security officers experienced physical or verbal abuse, and the industry welcomed MHA's commitment to amend the Private Security Industry Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: A survey conducted last year by the Union of Security Employees and the Singapore University of Social Sciences found that one in three security officers had experienced physical or verbal abuse or both in their course of work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: The security industry therefore welcomed MHA's commitment, announced last year, to amend the Private Security Industry Act to include safeguards for our security officers against abuse, as announced last year.

sections.label: New drug abusers under 30
sections.summary: The proportion of new abusers below 30 remained at 62% in 2020 and stayed consistent over the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Despite the CNB's herculean efforts in preventive drug education and many outreach activities and community engagement events, the proportion of new abusers below the age of 30 years remain at 62% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This statistic has been remained stubbornly consistent in the past five years: 2019 – 62%; 2018 – 64%; 2017 – 64% and 2016 – 66%.

sections.label: Youth views on drugs
sections.summary: Among youths aged 13 to 21, there is an upward trend towards a more liberal approach to drugs, and many wrongly perceive cannabis as less harmful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Among youths between 13 and 21 years old, there has been an upward trend in a more liberal approach towards drugs as an experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Furthermore, due to online sources and social media being the primary medium and source for information, a significant proportion of the youth perceive wrongly that cannabis is less harmful or non-addictive because of its medicinal uses.

sections.label: New psychoactive substances laws
sections.summary: Existing drug laws like the Misuse of Drugs Act must be flexible enough to make new psychoactive substances illegal before or soon after they appear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: With such a wide range of possible new psychoactive substances that could potentially appear on the Singapore market, our existing drug laws such as the Misuse of Drugs Act must be flexible enough to incorporate the new psychoactive substances and make them illegal to consume or traffic before or very soon after they appear within Singapore.

sections.label: Incarceration rate reduction question
sections.summary: The member asks whether such a system has been beneficial in reducing the incarceration rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Furthermore, I would like to ask if such a system has been beneficial in reducing the incarceration rate.

sections.label: FITRAH training and offender employment
sections.summary: The member asks if staff and volunteers will be trained for different offender demographics, noting about 10,000 inmates are released yearly and job retention rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I am grateful for the establishment of FITRAH, will the Government consider training staff and volunteers to be equipped for different demographics of offenders, for example, addicts or youths, and more targeted interventions to monitor and break inter-generational offenders?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Every year, about 10,000 inmates complete their sentence and are released.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Up to 2019, Yellow Ribbon Singapore (YRSG), formerly known as SCORE, has helped 96% of offenders in securing jobs with competitive salaries even before their release.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: However, only around 81% of them have retained their jobs within the first three months of release and another 64% within the first six months.

sections.label: Average prison offender population
sections.summary: Between 2018 and 2020, the average offender population in prison was 10,207 per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, between 2018 and 2020, the offender population in prison on the average is 10,207 per year.

sections.label: Ex-inmate jobs via Yellow Ribbon
sections.summary: 93% of inmates referred to Yellow Ribbon Singapore in 2020 secured a job prior to release.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: One of the best ways to encourage ex-inmates to turn over a new leaf is to get them decent jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I am heartened to note that 93% of inmates referred to Yellow Ribbon Singapore in 2020 secured a job prior to release.

sections.label: Scam growth and government spending
sections.summary: Scam cases grew 65%, over $200 million was siphoned across top 10 categories, and the Government should spend proportionately to mitigate this crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: Although the Government has moved quickly and substantially in this area by instituting the Protection from Harassment Act and other related measures, these harms are still experienced by many.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: On item (ae), Mr Chairman, I raised the point in my speech on the Budget Statement that the problem of scams is but a consequence of pursuing a digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: However, the steep growth rate of 65% in scam cases where the majority of the top 10 scam types relates to online scams is deeply concerning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: Given this rising trend where over $200 million has been siphoned across top 10 categories, it is reasonable for our Government to spend proportionately to mitigate this crime: one, to protect our residents who are digitally vulnerable; and two, to maintain the high trust levels in our Government.

sections.label: Private platforms and cross-border scam cooperation
sections.summary: The member asks whether the Ministry would rope in private sector platforms and increase cross-jurisdictional cooperation with neighbouring countries' law enforcement agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: Given the understanding of online fraud crime typologies and root causes, would the Ministry consider roping in relevant private sector platforms who have higher scam incidents and profit from the online eco-system to also step up and play their part in terms of fraud prevention and detection measures in the same way MAS is has engaged the banking sector?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: As such, will MHA increase cross jurisdictional cooperation with other neighbouring countries' law enforcement agencies to come up with a more comprehensive plan to combat this problem and to help the victims recover their monies?

sections.label: Pritam Singh's four points
sections.summary: Mr Pritam Singh raised four points: religious bias of top civil servants, the LGBTQ community, a Government statement on strict secularism, and updating the 1989 White Paper.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh, in his speech, quite an important speech, raised four points: one, possible religious bias of top civil servants now and in the future; two, our LGBTQ community; three, a possible Government statement on strict secularism; and fourth, updating the 1989 White Paper on Maintenance of Religious Harmony.

sections.label: Freedom of religion in public sphere
sections.summary: Freedom of religion is guaranteed, but in the public sphere and public policy-making, decisions do not favour any religious group.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Freedom of religion is guaranteed but in the public sphere, in public policy-making, we do not make decisions which favour anyone or other religious groups.

sections.label: secularity and religious neutrality principles
sections.summary: Secularity and neutrality between religions have been golden threads in public policy-making for the past 62 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The situation today, for the past 62 years, these principles – secularity, neutrality between religions, have been one of the golden threads in our public policy-making.

sections.label: Head of Civil Service praised
sections.summary: The current Head of Civil Service was the speaker's Permanent Secretary in Home Affairs, an outstanding officer of unimpeachable integrity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The current Head of Civil Service was my Permanent Secretary in Home Affairs – outstanding officer, unimpeachable integrity.

sections.label: leading pandemic response group
sections.summary: Since last year he has led the Homefront Crisis Executive Group, coordinating the pandemic response so Singaporeans can be safe.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Since last year, he has been working his guts out, leading the Homefront Crisis Executive Group (HCEG), coordinating and managing our pandemic response so that Singaporeans can be safe.

sections.label: assess work not religious beliefs
sections.summary: He will return to the Civil Service and should be assessed on his work quality, not his religious beliefs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: One day, he will go back to the Civil Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: He should be assessed on the basis of the quality of his work and not on the basis of the quality or nature of his religious beliefs.

sections.label: Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act amendments
sections.summary: MRHA amendments make urging violence on religious grounds an offence, covering attacks by religious groups on non-religious groups and vice versa.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act (MRHA) make it an offence to urge violence on the grounds of religion or religious belief, against any person or group.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Action can be taken under the MRHA where religious group, using religion, attacks a non-religious group, such as LGBT groups or individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Equally, where a religious group or its members is attacked by non-religious persons or groups, say LGBT, action can also be taken.

sections.label: equality of LGBTQ persons
sections.summary: LGBTQ persons and non-LGBTQ persons are all equal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: LGBTQ persons, non-LGBTQ persons – we are all equal.

sections.label: Religious and community groups commitment
sections.summary: Nearly 700 religious organisations, 680 exactly, and 73 community groups have affirmed this Commitment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: To date, nearly 700 religious organisations, 680 to be exact, and 73 community groups have affirmed this Commitment.

sections.label: MRHA amendments and religious harmony
sections.summary: Over 680 religious organisations committed to this call to action, and the MRHA was amended to strengthen religious harmony safeguards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: That more than 680 religious organisations have committed to this specific call to action, is to be celebrated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We amended the MRHA in several major aspects to strengthen our ability to safeguard against and respond more effectively to threats to our religious harmony.

sections.label: Higher standard for religious leaders
sections.summary: The amendments introduced a higher standard of behaviour for religious leaders because of their influence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The amendments also introduced a higher standard of behaviour for religious leaders, for example, because of the influence they can wield.

sections.label: No need for another White Paper
sections.summary: Given the many steps taken, there is no immediate need for another White Paper.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Given the many steps that have been taken, there is no immediate need for another White Paper.

sections.label: Transformation and technology use
sections.summary: Focus has been on transformation and increased technology use, including setting up HTX in December 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: To deal with this, we have been focusing on transformation and increased the use of technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: To start with we set up the Home Team Science and Technology agency HTX, in December 2019, to develop customised tech solutions for our needs, better use tech, reduce some types of work, multiply our capabilities.

sections.label: Police cameras in public locations
sections.summary: Police installed almost 90,000 cameras in major public locations, assisting in solving nearly 5,000 cases as of December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Police have installed almost 90,000 cameras in major public locations – HDB estates, neighbourhood centres and carparks.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As of December 2020, police cameras have assisted in solving nearly 5,000 cases; 4,900 to be precise.

sections.label: Police next-generation Fast Response Cars
sections.summary: Police will roll out 300 next-generation Fast Response Cars by 2023, within the next two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Three, Police will roll out 300 next-generation Fast Response Cars (FRCs) by 2023; within the next two years.

sections.label: Multimodal Biometric System immigration clearance
sections.summary: Eligible travellers can already use the Multimodal Biometric System to clear immigration by scanning their face and iris.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: First, today, eligible travellers can already use what we call the Multimodal Biometric System to clear immigration by scanning their face and iris.

sections.label: ICA enhanced e-services
sections.summary: ICA has enhanced its e-services, allowing automatic processing of many applications and reducing manual handling by ICA officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second, ICA has enhanced its e-services, which will allow it to automatically process many of the applications and significantly reduce the volume of applications which have to be dealt with by ICA officers manually.

sections.label: Prisons Without Guards strategy
sections.summary: Prisons has made good progress with tech, in particular the Prisons Without Guards strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Prisons has also made good progress with tech, in particular, what they call the “Prisons Without Guards” strategy.

sections.label: Prisons digital watch tracking device
sections.summary: Prisons is developing a tracking device that looks like a digital watch.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Prisons is developing a tracking device that looks like a digital watch.

sections.label: Police HTX XENTINEL rogue drones
sections.summary: Police and HTX are developing XENTINEL, a mobile vehicle platform to detect, track and safely take down rogue drones from a long distance.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Police and HTX are developing the XENTINEL, which is a mobile vehicle platform that can be quickly deployed to detect, track and safely take down rogue drones from a long distance.

sections.label: ICA digital documents
sections.summary: ICA will issue more document types digitally, including birth and death certificates and long-term passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: ICA will be issuing more types of documents in digital form, such as birth and death certificates, and long-term passes.

sections.label: New Integrated Services Centre
sections.summary: ICA is building a new Integrated Services Centre beside the existing ICA Building for counter services.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: ICA is Building a new Integrated Services Centre next to the existing ICA Building to provide counter services.

sections.label: Integrated Services Centre construction
sections.summary: Construction of the Integrated Services Centre has started and is targeted for completion by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Construction works for the Integrated Services Centre has commenced and is targeted for completion by 2023.

sections.label: Home Team Academy technology enhancements
sections.summary: The Home Team Academy will add technologies like artificial intelligence, and SCDF's Civil Defence Academy re-development includes a Digital Learning Lab and Virtual Reality training; HTX will hire scientists and engineers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Home Team Academy will enhance the system with new technologies like artificial intelligence and expand the usage by officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: SCDF’s re-development of the Civil Defence Academy will include a Digital Learning Lab and it will provide Virtual Reality training for SCDF officers, such as extricating people from a car wreckage.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: HTX will need to hire a few hundred scientists and engineers over the next few years to build a critical mass of experts in areas like digital and crime scene forensics, robotics and automation.

sections.label: Singapore law and order rankings
sections.summary: The 2020 Gallup Global Law and Order Report ranked Singapore first for the seventh year, and the 2020 World Justice Project Rule of Law Index ranked Singapore first for Order and Security.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The 2020 Gallup Global Law and Order Report ranked Singapore first, for the seventh year running.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Singapore was also ranked first in the 2020 World Justice Project Rule of Law Index in the area of “Order and Security”.

sections.label: Residents trust Home Team
sections.summary: In the most recent survey, nine in 10 Singapore residents agreed the Home Team has done well and trust officers to serve with integrity.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the most recent survey, nine in 10 Singapore residents agreed that the Home Team has done well and trust our officers to serve them with integrity.

sections.label: ISD and Batam plot
sections.summary: ISD worked with Indonesian authorities to disrupt a Batam-based pro-ISIS cell targeting Marina Bay Sands.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, ISD worked closely with the Indonesian authorities to disrupt the plot by a Batam-based pro-ISIS cell targeting Marina Bay Sands.

sections.label: Cyber-enabled election interference increase
sections.summary: Cyber-enabled foreign interference in elections rose from seven cases in 2011-2015 to 41 in 2016-2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Globally, cases of cyber-enabled foreign interference in elections increased from seven between 2011 and 2015, to 41 between 2016 and 2020.

sections.label: Measures against foreign subversion
sections.summary: Recent experiences of other countries mean further measures are needed against foreign subversion of politically significant individuals and entities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Given the recent experiences of other countries, we need to consider further measures to guard against foreign subversion of politically significant individuals and entities.

sections.label: Internet and harmful content
sections.summary: The Internet makes spreading harmful content quick and easy, including violent extremist propaganda that radicalised a 16-year-old detained last year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Indeed, the Internet has made dissemination of harmful content quick and easy, in ways previously not possible.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Such harmful content includes violent extremist propaganda, such as the livestreaming of the 2019 shootings in Christchurch and the shooter's manifesto, which radicalised the 16-year-old detained last year.

sections.label: Germany platform complaint legislation
sections.summary: Germany has passed legislation requiring platforms to respond to user complaints about unlawful content.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, Germany has passed legislation requiring platforms to respond to user complaints about unlawful content.

sections.label: Video Recording of interviews expansion
sections.summary: VRI has been gradually expanded since its introduction in 2018, in response to a question about implementation and interpreters.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Mr Leong Mun Wai asked about the implementation of Video Recording of interviews (VRI) and increasing the pool of foreign language interpreters for police interviews.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We have gradually expanded VRI since introducing it in 2018.

sections.label: Police interpreters for foreign languages
sections.summary: The Police currently engage interpreters for foreign languages.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Police currently engage the services of interpreters for foreign languages.

sections.label: UN vote on cannabis scheduling
sections.summary: Last December, the UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs narrowly voted to remove cannabis and cannabis resin from Schedule IV of the 1961 Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Last December, the UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs narrowly voted to remove cannabis and cannabis resin from Schedule IV of the 1961 Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, which lists the most dangerous drugs.

sections.label: CNB seizures and NPS regulation
sections.summary: In 2020 CNB seized about $11.6 million worth of drugs, and this year the Act will be amended to regulate NPS by psychoactive effect potential.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In 2020, CNB seized about $11.6 million worth of drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Home Team intercepted 568 parcels containing suspected drugs and related paraphernalia, many of which were online purchases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Currently, because of how NPS are listed in the Misuse of Drugs Act, there may be a time lag from detecting to listing a novel NPS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This year, we will amend the Act to regulate NPS based on their potential to produce a psychoactive effect to allow CNB to take swifter enforcement action.

sections.label: EDRR recidivism rate study
sections.summary: A Prisons study found the two-year recidivism rate for drug abusers who went through the EDRR was eight percentage points lower.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: A Prisons study revealed that the two-year recidivism rate for drug abusers who went through the EDRR was eight percentage points lower than those who did not.

sections.label: Yellow Ribbon Singapore career masterplan
sections.summary: YRSG has charted a career masterplan, and under a Train and Place and Grow initiative partners will offer employment and upgrading after release.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Yellow Ribbon Singapore or YRSG, previously known as SCORE, has charted a career masterplan to train inmates for careers in key and growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Under a new Train and Place (TAP) and Grow initiative, partner industries and training providers will offer employment and continuous upgrading through a work-study arrangement after inmates' release.

sections.label: Jobs Growth Incentive for ex-offenders
sections.summary: Under the Jobs Growth Incentive launched in September, ex-offenders are eligible for the higher tier of wage support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Under the Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI) that was launched in September, ex-offenders are eligible for the higher tier of wage support.

sections.label: Inmate employment assistance outcomes
sections.summary: From 2018 to 2020, an average of 2,560 inmates received employment assistance before release yearly, and about 95% of those assisted secured a job.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2020, an average of 2,560 inmates received employment assistance prior to release each year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In all, about 95% of all who received assistance between 2018 and 2020 secured a job.

sections.label: Scam cases reported in 2020
sections.summary: In 2020, more than 15,000 scam cases were reported, a 65% increase from 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In 2020, more than 15,000 cases of scams were reported, a 65% increase from 2019.

sections.label: Freezing suspected scam bank accounts
sections.summary: Once notified, Police can swiftly freeze most suspected scam bank accounts within a day, down from 14 to 60 working days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Once the Police are notified, most bank accounts suspected to be involved in scammers' operations can be swiftly frozen within a day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: This is a big step forward from the 14 to 60 working days that these tasks used to take.

sections.label: Age of scam victims in 2020
sections.summary: MHA's survey found that in 2020, close to 50% of scam victims were between 20 and 39 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: MHA's survey found that in 2020, close to 50% of scam victims were between 20 and 39 years old.

sections.label: ScamShield blocking and filtering
sections.summary: To date, ScamShield is actively blocking over 2,500 scam numbers and has filtered more than 280,000 scam messages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To date, ScamShield is actively blocking over 2,500 scam numbers and has filtered more than 280,000 scam messages.

sections.label: New offences for abusing security officers
sections.summary: MHA will amend the Private Security Industry Act to include new offences with harsher penalties for verbal and physical abuse of security officers on duty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: MHA takes a very serious view on the abuse of security officers and we will amend the Private Security Industry Act, or PSIA, to include new offences to address the common types of verbal and physical abuse which security officers face when carrying out their duties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: These offences will also carry harsher penalties, compared to similar offences against the general public.

sections.label: Road traffic fatalities decline
sections.summary: Road traffic fatalities fell from 195 in 2011 to 118 in 2019 and 85 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Road traffic fatalities have decreased in the past decade, from 195 in 2011 to 118 in 2019, and 85 last year in 2020.

sections.label: Penalties at pedestrian crossings
sections.summary: Penalties will increase for motorists committing offences at pedestrian crossings or endangering pedestrians in Silver Zones, with similar measures for School Zones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: For example, to better protect elderly pedestrians, we will increase the penalties for motorists who commit offences at pedestrian crossings or offences that endanger pedestrian safety in Silver Zones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We will also put in place similar measures for School Zones to protect students.

sections.label: Equality for LGBT persons
sections.summary: A Minister said LGBT and non-LGBT persons are all equal, and the speaker hopes Singaporeans have respectful conversations on LGBTQ issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The second point, I think it was an important remark that Minister made, which was with regard to the point on LGBT and non-LGBT persons and that they are all equal and no one is any lesser compared to the other.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I think it is a very powerful statement – a fair and egalitarian approach to dealing with the matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And I hope all Singaporeans, regardless of race or religion, actually coalesce around this and have reasoned and respectful conversations on LGBTQ issues, and I think we will be stronger as a nation for it.

sections.label: Number of cameras installed
sections.summary: The speaker said 90,000 cameras are already installed and more will follow, depending on MOF.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the third point, I did not say 90,000 more.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I said 90,000 cameras are already installed and there are going to be many more, and how many more depends on the kindness of MOF.

sections.label: Ages of radicalised persons
sections.summary: The speaker notes the ages of those identified as radicalised have gone down quite a lot over the last decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Has there been a drop because of COVID-19?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is of great concern to us because, if you look at the pattern, what has changed over the last decade or so is that, amongst those that we have found to be radicalised, the ages of those who have been identified have gone down quite a lot.

sections.label: Rehabilitation of radicalised youths
sections.summary: Most of the seven self-radicalised youths aged 16 to 19 dealt with under the ISA since 2015 have made good progress in rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Among the seven self-radicalised youths aged between 16 and 19 that were dealt with under the ISA since 2015, most have made good progress in their rehabilitation.

sections.label: Inmate employment assistance and virtual interviews
sections.summary: About 2,520 inmates secured jobs yearly through employment assistance, and about 690 did so via virtual job interviews after COVID-19 measures.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Minister of State, would you like to remove your mask?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, about 2,520 inmates secured jobs each year after receiving the employment assistance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We were also fortunate that shortly after the introduction of COVID-19 Safe Management Measures, YRSG went into virtual job interviews.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We were able to successfully assist about 690 inmates to secure jobs via virtual job interviews.

sections.label: Criminalising NPS enforcement powers
sections.summary: The Ministry is looking at empowering CNB to act against illicit NPS activities by criminalising substances capable of producing a psychoactive effect, unless exempted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Essentially, we know some of the limitations or constraints of the current approach and we are looking at how we can empower CNB to take enforcement action against illicit activities involving NPS that are not yet listed as controlled drugs, by criminalising all such activities involving substances capable of producing a psychoactive effect, unless they are exempted.

sections.label: Balancing business and targeting NPS
sections.summary: Legislation to be shared in the next few months will include elements from a law balancing legitimate business and scientific interest while targeting NPS meant for abuse.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: How they have done so in terms of striking a balance between legitimate business and also commercial and scientific interest and target NPS that have been developed to exhibit properties similar to controlled drugs – and are meant for abuse.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, our legislation that we will be sharing and placing in the next few months, we will share some elements found in this law.

sections.label: Monitoring intergenerational offending and incarcerated parents
sections.summary: A question asked what steps the Ministry would consider to monitor and break intergenerational offending, including cases where both parents are incarcerated and children are involved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: My second point is, I would very much like to ask what steps the Ministry is willing to consider, to monitor and break intergenerational offending, and also in cases where both parents are incarcerated when there are children involved.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, as I mentioned earlier in my speech, this year, Prisons will work with MSF to share some of these data.

sections.label: Rolling out pilot to FSCs
sections.summary: A pilot will be rolled out to Family Service Centres across Singapore to have more such interventions to help families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Essentially, we had a pilot, and we are going to roll this out to the FSCs across Singapore and to see how we can have more of such interventions to help the families.
